title: Staging Daily Closes (per-row record)
description: staging/daily_closes/{date}.parquet — one row per ticker, written by collectors/daily_closes.py::collect(). The parquet is intermediate state (7-day S3 lifecycle expiry), consumed by builders/daily_append.py (ArcticDB ingest) and crucible-executor/executor/upstream_artifact_gate.py (freshness only, no column pin). This schema validates ONE ROW after `df.reset_index().to_dict('records')` — the persisted artifact is the parquet, not a JSON document; the row shape is the contract. v1 adds `source` (already persisted) and `revision` (alpha-engine-config-I10783, additive) so the write records which vendor produced each cell and how many times it has been overwritten, instead of a silent overwrite between vendors. Mirrors sources/contract.py::PriceBar.RECORD_KEYS and sources/SCHEMA.md §2, which remain the authoritative field catalog (this schema is a data-collector-plan-P-16 restatement of that catalog for consumer pinning). PRODUCER TEST: tests/test_staging_daily_closes_contract.py.

x-settling-bar.rationale: The file is indexed by TICKER, not by date: the whole artifact IS one trading day's bar, named by the date in its own key. When that date is the report's trading_day every value cell in it is the unsettled bar, so the whole file is graded as settling rather than row-by-row. Membership (the ticker set), schema and row count stay strict (alpha-engine-config-I11351).

ticker.description: Canonical store-key (dash form for US class shares, e.g. BRK-B; caret-stripped for index tickers, e.g. VIX not ^VIX).

Close.description: Price, native currency. Null Close is treated as missing by the source-priority coalesce.

Adj_Close.description: Split/dividend-adjusted close where the source provides one (yfinance); equals Close where it does not (polygon, FRED).

Volume.description: Raw shares. 0 when the source carries no volume (FRED single-value closes).

VWAP.description: True volume-weighted price. Null when the source can't provide it — never a (H+L+C)/3 proxy.

source.description: Provenance — the vendor that WON this cell under collectors.daily_closes.VENDOR_PRECEDENCE (the declared, reversible champion pointer; polygon is champion per the 2026-09-09 ruling). Not necessarily the only vendor that supplied a value this trading day — see data_collection/metrics/vendor_divergence/{date}.json for the cross-vendor comparison.

revision.description: Per-cell write counter, default 1. Incremented only when an existing cell is actually overwritten by an equal-or-higher-priority source (collectors.daily_closes._coalesce_by_source_priority) — an explicit, queryable trail of vendor overwrites instead of a silent one (alpha-engine-config-I10783). x-provenance (alpha-engine-config-I10894): a run-identity counter, not a data value — shadow/parity.py excludes it from `values.breaches` and reports it under `provenance_diffs` instead, because it is DEFINED to differ between the live and shadow read-modify-write chains (I10891).

xsource_provenance.description: Cross-source observer audit string (collectors/cross_source_observer.py XSOURCE_PROVENANCE, built by sources/cross_source_gate.py as GateDecision.provenance), e.g. `A@2026-09-22: yfinance=167.2700 single-source PROVISIONAL (no cross-check)`. Optional: only the L1 observer writes it. x-provenance (alpha-engine-config-I11559): the text EMBEDS the vendor and price the row was built from, so grading it as data re-grades the same `Close` a second time, as a string, with no tolerance. shadow/parity.py reports it under `provenance_diffs` instead of `values.breaches`. The price it embeds is still graded, strictly, in its own `Close` column, and the vendor in `source`.
